title: SLI Sensitivity Lab: Catalog, Simulation Procedures, and Notes
author: Priya Desai
content:
Overview

Purpose: This page catalogs the SLI sensitivity experiments we run in the Platform SLI Lab, documents reproducible simulation procedures, and captures pragmatic notes for dashboarding and alert-tuning. The lab helps answer: how does varying traffic mix, batching, and cache hit rate affect our SLO attainment and alert signal fidelity?

Scope: Platform services (inference-router, batcher, kv-prefix-cache, tenant-allocator). This is not an application-level SLI guide — refer to the service-specific SLI pages for per-service definitions.

When to use this document
- Pre-rollout validation for routing/priority changes.
- Alerting threshold calibration (reduce false positives during controlled degradation).
- Capacity planning and tenant burst experiments.

Experiment Catalog (summary table)
| Experiment name | Goal | Primary owner | Last run | Artifact location | Notes |
| SLI-Noise-Inject-Uniform | Measure false-positive rate under small latency noise | Priya Desai | 2026-02-14 | s3://redwood-lab/sli-noise/uniform-20260214.tar.gz | Injects 50–150ms tail jitter on a subset of hosts |
| Batch-Sensitivity-Profile | Quantify throughput/latency tradeoffs for batch sizes 1-64 | Marcus Nguyen | 2026-01-20 | s3://redwood-lab/batching/batch-profile-20260120.tar.gz | Includes kernel-level telemetry for GPU/CPU |
| KVCache-Hit-Decay | Simulate progressive cache-thrashing and SLO impact | Elena Alvarez | 2026-02-05 | s3://redwood-lab/kv-cache/decay-20260205.tar.gz | Uses synthetic prefix workloads and TTL variance |
| Priority-Rebalance-Drain | Measure SLO outcomes during tenant priority rebalance | Ravi Shah | 2026-02-02 | s3://redwood-lab/priority/rebalance-20260202.tar.gz | Emulates tenant burst credits and eviction policies |

Experiment Artifact Standard
- Each experiment directory must include: README.md, runbook.log, terraform.tfstate (if infra changes), prometheus_exporter_snapshot.json, grafana-dashboard.json, analysis.ipynb.
- Naming convention: <experiment>-YYYYMMDD.tar.gz

Prerequisites and Safety Controls
1) Environment: Use the lab namespace (k8s namespace: platform-sli-lab). Do NOT run in prod clusters.
2) Access: Only members of the Platform Lab group may trigger experiments (IAM role: platform-lab-runner).
3) Quotas: Verify GPU and node quotas prior to running. Persona: platform-ops oncall must be paged 30 minutes prior to long-running experiments (>2h).
4) Canary gating: For experiments that touch routing/fallbacks, create a canary route and a short-lived experiment token to avoid cross-tenant bleed.

Standard simulation procedure (canonical)
1) Prepare baseline snapshot
   - Export current dashboards: curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" $GRAFANA/api/dashboards/db/platform-sli | jq . > baseline_grafana.json
   - Snapshot prometheus metrics: python tools/snapshot_prometheus.py --out baseline_prom.json --query-config baseline_queries.yml
2) Provision lab infra (example commands)
   - terraform workspace select lab || terraform workspace new lab
   - terraform apply -var-file=lab.tfvars -auto-approve
3) Deploy controlled traffic generator
   - kubectl -n platform-sli-lab apply -f k8s/traffic-generator.yaml
   - Validate generator: kubectl -n platform-sli-lab logs deploy/traffic-gen --tail=50
4) Run the experiment (example: Batch-Sensitivity-Profile)
   - python scripts/simulate_batching.py --target inference-router:8080 --batch-sizes 1 2 4 8 16 32 64 --duration 3600 --out ./results/batch-profile.json
   - Monitor core metrics: token_latency_p50/p90/p99, request_count, batch_size_distribution, gpu_utilization_percent
5) Controlled perturbations
   - For cache experiments: python scripts/kv_cache_thrash.py --hot-keys 1000 --ttl-ms 500 --rps 2000
   - For routing experiments: apply traffic-weight mutation: kubectl -n platform apply -f experiments/routing-weight-change.yaml
6) Data collection and teardown
   - Gather Prometheus snapshots and exporter logs: python tools/collect_artifacts.py --out s3://redwood-lab/<experiment>-$(date +%Y%m%d).tar.gz
   - terraform destroy -var-file=lab.tfvars -auto-approve
   - Upload runbook.log with operator notes and incident markers

How to interpret results (quick checklist)
- Compare p99 shifts relative to baseline: p99_delta_ms = p99_experiment - p99_baseline. If p99_delta_ms > 0.5 * SLO_latency_ms, flag for follow-up.
- SLI noise floor: compute false-positive rate by replaying alert rules against baseline and experiment traces. Aim for <2% increase in false positives.
- Cost delta: estimate incremental GPU hours and projected monthly cost for scaled pattern.

Example thresholds and actions
| Metric | Threshold (example) | Recommended action | Owner |
| p99 latency increase | > 50% of SLO | Halt rollout; open bug; priority incident | Platform SRE |
| Increase in alert rate | > 3× baseline | Reduce alert sensitivity; re-evaluate query; schedule calmer window | Observability team |
| Batch size variance | > 2× expected | Revert batch-tuning changes; inspect kernel backpressure | Runtime team |

Dashboard template (panels to include)
- Latency panel: p50/p90/p99 (lines) with baseline overlay.
- Latency heatmap: token-level latency by step (encode/attend/decode).
- Batch distribution histogram.
- Cache hit-rate timeseries + eviction rate.
- Tenant-level SLO attainment table (tenant, p99_latency_ms, error_rate, tokens).
- Cost estimate panel: extrapolated GPU hours and token cost.

Alert tuning guidance (practical rules)
1) Avoid raw p99 alerts without context: combine with increased request rate or reduced cache hit-rate. Example: alert when p99> X AND req_rate > Y.
2) Use rolling-window evaluation for SLI alerts (3-minute and 1-hour smoothed rules) to reduce flapping.
3) Tag alerts with experiment-run id: label experiment_id to suppress noisy alerts during an active experiment.

Runbook: During an active experiment (critical steps)
1) Confirm experiment_id and contact list.
2) Monitor the experiment dashboard and the global SLI dashboard.
3) If p99_delta_ms crosses the actionable threshold:
   a) Pause the generator: kubectl -n platform-sli-lab scale deploy/traffic-gen --replicas=0
   b) Snapshot exporters and logs: python tools/collect_artifacts.py --out /tmp/hot-snapshot.tar.gz
   c) Revert any temporary routing rules: kubectl apply -f experiments/routing-rollback.yaml
   d) Notify Platform SRE and the experiment owner via PagerDuty and Slack channel #platform-sli-lab
4) After stabilization, run a postmortem checklist (see Retrospective Checklist below).

Ownership and contact matrix
- Experiment owner (author): listed in the Catalog table. Primary contact for hypothesis and artifacts.
- Platform SRE: PagerDuty (team) and channel #platform-sre.
- Observability: Slack #observability, oncall rotation in rota-observability.

Retrospective Checklist (post-experiment)
1) Document hypothesis vs. findings in runbook.log.
2) Attach artifacts (dashboards, notebooks) to the experiment wiki entry.
3) Update any affected alert thresholds in the staging alert repo and run synthetic test.
4) If a change is promoted to prod, run the canary gating plan and notify compliance for private deployments.

Common pitfalls and mitigation notes
- Pitfall: Invisible tail effects due to sampling in exporters. Mitigation: increase exporter sample rate and annotate dashboards with sampling fraction.
- Pitfall: Cross-tenant bleed when synthetic tenants are not isolated. Mitigation: use tenant scoping in tenant-allocator to pin synthetic load to lab node pools.

Quick utilities and snippets
- Start a short smoke sim: python scripts/simulate_batching.py --target inference-router:8080 --batch-sizes 1 8 16 --duration 300 --out ./tmp/smoke.json
- Pause experimental traffic generator: kubectl -n platform-sli-lab scale deploy/traffic-gen --replicas=0
- Snapshot prometheus: python tools/snapshot_prometheus.py --out ./snap.json --duration 600

Governance and promotion path
- All experiments that intend to change alert rules or SLOs must include: hypothesis, prometheus queries, simulated traffic config, and an owner.
- Changes to production SLOs require: experimental evidence + approval from Platform SRE manager and Product (email thread and short review).

Related pages and artifacts
- Tokenized SLI design patterns and dashboard library (see related pages).
- Platform SLI lab infra repo: git@github.com:redwood/platform-sli-lab.git
